ui.title: EasyShoot user guide: every feature, one topic at a time
ui.description: The EasyShoot user guide for Mac: setup, capture, Quick Access, markup tools, styles, pixelate and blur, text, backgrounds, presets, export, shortcuts, settings and privacy.
ui.intro: Everything EasyShoot can do, one topic at a time. Start at the top, or jump to what you need.

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.short: Install, allow screen capture and take your first screenshot.
getting-started.description: Install EasyShoot on your Mac, allow Screen Recording and take your first screenshot.
getting-started.intro: EasyShoot works on any Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

blocks.html:
• Get EasyShoot from the Mac App Store.
  • Open it. The Welcome window asks for Screen Recording, which every screenshot needs. Click Allow…, turn on EasyShoot in the list, then press Restart.
  • EasyShoot lives in the menu bar. Click its icon and choose Capture Area…, or press ⌥⇧⌘4.
If the notch hides the menu bar icon, use the shortcuts. To see the Welcome window again, open EasyShoot from the Applications folder.

capture.title: Capture
capture.short: Area, window, full screen, or an image you already have.
capture.description: Capture an area, a window or the full screen on your Mac with EasyShoot, or open a copied image or a file in the editor.
capture.intro: Each kind of capture has its own shortcut. The defaults use Option-Shift-Command so they never clash with the Mac's own.

blocks.html:
CaptureShortcut
Area: drag over what you want⌥⇧⌘4
Window: click a window⌥⇧⌘5
Fullscreen⌥⇧⌘3
Annotate Clipboard Image⌥⇧⌘7
Open Image…: edit a file⌘O
To leave the window's shadow out of window captures, turn off Include window shadow in Settings › General.

quick-access.title: Quick Access
quick-access.short: What happens right after a capture.
quick-access.description: Quick Access in EasyShoot: copy, save, edit or drag a screenshot right after you take it, and choose what happens after every capture.
quick-access.intro: After every capture, Quick Access shows a thumbnail in the corner of the screen. Copy it, save it, open it in the editor or drag it straight into another app.

blocks.html:
Settings › General › After capture decides what happens on its own:

  • Copy to clipboard
  • Save to folder
  • Open the editor immediately
  • Show Quick Access overlay
  • Play sound

Close Quick Access after sets how long the thumbnail stays: never, 5, 10 or 30 seconds.

mark-up.title: Mark up
mark-up.short: Arrows, shapes, numbered steps, text and pen.
mark-up.description: The EasyShoot markup tools and their keys: arrow, line, rectangle, diamond, ellipse, numbered steps, text and pen.
mark-up.intro: Every tool is one key away, so you can point and explain without reaching for the toolbar.

blocks.alt: The EasyShoot editor with a box, two numbered steps, an arrow and a note on a checkout page.
blocks.html:
• Arrow · ADrag to draw; drag the middle handle to bend it.
  • Line · LA straight line between two points.
  • Rectangle · RBox the part that matters.
  • Diamond · DA shape that stands out from boxes.
  • Ellipse · OCircle a number or a button.
  • Numbered step · NClick in order: 1, 2, 3 count themselves.
  • Text · TA short note right where it's needed.
  • Pen · PDraw by hand.
Press V to select. Drag a mark to move it, drag a handle to resize it, and press Delete to remove it. Every mark stays editable until you export.

styles.title: Styles
styles.short: Colour, stroke, fill, edges, angle and opacity.
styles.description: Style any mark in EasyShoot: colour, stroke width, solid, dashed or dotted lines, fills, rounded edges, angle, opacity and shadow.
styles.intro: The Style tab in the inspector follows the tool in your hand or the mark you selected, and shows only what that mark uses.

blocks.alt: The Style tab with a dashed, filled box and a dotted ellipse on the screenshot.
blocks.html:
• Stroke and widthFive colours, or more in the colour picker. Thin, medium or bold, or any width from 1 to 30.
  • Stroke styleSolid, dashed or dotted lines and shapes.
  • BackgroundA light fill for rectangles, diamonds, ellipses and numbered steps.
  • Edges and angleSharp or round corners. Type an angle or turn the handle; Shift snaps to 15°.
  • Arrow headStandard or swept.
  • Opacity and shadowFade any mark, and add a soft shadow if you want one.
Press ⌘A, Shift-click, or drag a box over empty canvas to select several marks. Move, restyle or delete them together; a change applies only the setting you touched.

hide-details.title: Hide private details
hide-details.short: Pixelate or blur emails, names and card numbers.
hide-details.description: Pixelate or blur private details in a screenshot on your Mac with EasyShoot before you share it.
hide-details.intro: Hide what isn't yours to share before the image leaves your Mac.

blocks.alt: A card number blurred with the Pixelate tool, and the Style tab set to Blur.
blocks.html:
• Press B or pick Pixelate.
  • Drag over the email, card number or face.
  • In the Style tab choose Pixels or Blur and set the Strength.

The exported image keeps only the hidden version, not the original detail.

text.title: Text
text.short: Any font, three looks, and right-to-left text.
text.description: Add text to screenshots with EasyShoot: any Mac or Google font, plain, bubble or outline, and Arabic or Hebrew right to left.
text.intro: Press T, click where the note goes and type.

blocks.alt: A note in a bubble on the screenshot, with the Style tab showing font, size, look and direction.
blocks.html:
• FontAny font on your Mac, or a Google font downloaded the moment you pick it.
  • SizeUse the slider, or drag the text's corner.
  • LookPlain, Bubble or Outline.
  • DirectionAuto writes Arabic and Hebrew right to left with letters joined correctly; LTR or RTL forces a line.

background-and-crop.title: Background and crop
background-and-crop.short: Frame a shot, crop it and resize it.
background-and-crop.description: Put a screenshot on a background with padding, rounded corners and shadow in EasyShoot, then crop and resize it.
background-and-crop.intro: The Background tab makes a capture ready to post.

blocks.alt: The screenshot on a soft gradient, with fill, padding, corner radius and shadow in the Background tab.
blocks.html: Pick a gradient, a solid colour, your own colour or none, then set padding, corner radius, shadow, aspect ratio and alignment.

• Crop · CFree, or fixed at 1:1, 4:3 or 16:9.
  • ResizeBy percent, or to an exact width.
  • Zoom⌘+ and ⌘− for small details; ⌘0 shows actual size and ⌘9 fits the window.

presets.title: Presets
presets.short: Save a look and reuse it.
presets.description: Save a background, mark style and export settings as a preset in EasyShoot, and make it the default.
presets.intro: A preset keeps a background, a mark style and export settings together.

blocks.html:
• To save one, open Presets in the editor's toolbar and choose Save Current Style as Preset….
  • To use one, pick it from the same menu.
  • In Settings › Presets, choose Make Default so every new screenshot starts with it, or Restore Built-in Presets.

With no default, each screenshot starts with the settings you used last.

export.title: Export and share
export.description: Copy or save screenshots from EasyShoot as PNG, JPEG, HEIC or TIFF, at any size, or drag them into another app.
export.intro: Copy, save or drag the image straight into Messages, Slack or Mail.

blocks.html:
ActionShortcut
Copy the image⇧⌘C
Save⌘S
The Export tab sets the Format (PNG, JPEG, HEIC or TIFF), the quality and the size. Choose the Save location in Settings › General, and turn on Close the editor after copying to finish in one step.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.description: Every EasyShoot keyboard shortcut: global capture shortcuts, editor tools and editor commands.
shortcuts.intro: Change the capture shortcuts in Settings › Shortcuts. The editor keys work whenever you're not typing text.

settings.title: Settings
settings.short: General, Shortcuts, Presets, Permissions and About.
settings.description: What each part of EasyShoot's Settings does: General, Shortcuts, Presets, Permissions and About.
settings.intro: Open Settings… from the menu bar icon, or press ⌘, while EasyShoot is in front.

blocks.html:
• GeneralWhat happens after capture, the save location, window shadow, editor options and update notices.
  • ShortcutsRecord your own capture shortcuts.
  • PresetsRename, delete, make default or restore the built-in presets.
  • PermissionsCheck Screen Recording, which every screenshot needs.
  • AboutVersion, website and support.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.short: What stays on your Mac, and when the app goes online.
privacy.description: How EasyShoot handles privacy: no account, no cloud, no tracking, and the two times it goes online.
privacy.intro: No account, no cloud and no tracking. Your screenshots stay on your Mac and go only where you copy, save or drag them.

blocks.html:
• To download a Google font you pick for text.
  • To check the App Store for a newer version. Turn this off with Tell me when an update is available in Settings › General.
Read the full privacy policy.
